Yes, that direction is right. The essential first version is quick saving, automatically filling in recognizable page details, a readable list, strong search, tags, and a clear way to separate unread, finished, and archived links. I also need to be able to correct or add details and notes after saving. If I accidentally save the same address again, I’d expect to be taken to the existing entry instead of ending up with duplicates.

Preserving a local copy of the page is important to the long-term goal, but it can come after that basic experience is solid. Importing my existing browser bookmarks would also be useful later.

I picture using it mainly in a web browser on my computer. It should still be comfortable on a phone for quickly saving or looking up a link, but I don’t need a separate mobile app.
